premise: I cashed out my $126,000 401(k) to buy and restore a 1950s Airstream trailer fleet for a mobile vintage glamour studio with my half‑sister, who notarized a 50/50 share and promised me a lifetime of free up‑dos for my granddaughters’ weddings; after a wedding‑planning franchise bid $870,000 for the branded fleet, she forged an ownership transfer, sold the trailers, and gave me a $4,500 “retro” compact mirror—I discovered the original partnership document inside a hidden compartment of a restored trailer’s upholstery, voided the sale, and now run ‘Trailer of Betrayal Glam,’ where she sanitizes curling irons in a smock that reads ‘Curling Lies’ and every appointment card prints the fraud docket number.
